conventions.bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1], fractions of the PDF page (A4, incl. the white frame around the scan)

drawings.description: à droite de ces formules, un croquis : une région $C$ hachurée par deux familles de droites parallèles. Le signe devant $\operatorname{bnd}_D$ est bien une intersection sur la page, là où l'on attendrait une réunion
drawings.kind: region hatched by two families of parallel lines
drawings.notes: Re-read on a zoomed view: five descending and five rising lines (the outer ones short), each drawn once from end to end, so that every crossing of the hatching is the crossing of the lines themselves; the first descending line starts on the upper arm of the brace on the left. The faint wavy outline is drawn in its separate pieces (left loop, top arc, top right, the bottom C-shaped piece, the loop at the bottom, the bottom right wave). The families are not quite parallel on the page, and several lines bend a little: they are drawn as he drew them. The small marks inside the region (four short signs, one perhaps a letter) are not read and are left out: the transcription names no label there and the formulas beside the sketch already name the region C (settled 2026-11-12, no consequence); the label C is not on the sketch. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 250 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session); each line was checked by sampling the ink across it at nine points. Six of the ten lines were straight segments 1 to 2 units off their ink (the second rising line up to 2.5 units, and it runs on at the top past the crossing with the fourth descending line to a small hook, which was missing): they are redrawn as polylines through the ink, the second rising line extended to its end; the other four and the outline pieces lie on their ink within about 1 unit. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, un croquis : une bande entre deux droites parallèles, un point marqué sur l'une, et une ligne brisée en zigzag entre les deux
drawings.kind: strip between two parallel lines with a zigzag
drawings.notes: Two nearly parallel lines bounding a strip, a marked point on the upper one (left end) with a tick to the right; from the point a broken zigzag line runs between the two lines (shape approximate).

drawings.description: après « qui n'est pas un parallélogramme », un petit croquis à l'encre épaisse : un quadrilatère, et deux traits issus de ses deux sommets de gauche qui se rejoignent en un point au-dessus de son côté supérieur.
drawings.kind: quadrilateral with two strokes meeting outside it
drawings.notes: A very small, heavily inked sketch (about 8 mm wide), its strokes blotted to 3 or 4 units wide. Drawn on the centre line of the ink: the quadrilateral (a long bottom side, a short right side with a small tail at its foot, a long top side sloping down to the right, the left side) and two heavy strokes from its two left vertices which meet at a point above the top side: the upper one straight, the lower one crossing the top side and turning up through a small loop to that point. Left out: the tails of two letters of the line above, which come down to that point, and a short stroke above the upper left vertex (also part of the writing). The figure is the transcription's: a quadrilateral that is not a parallelogram and two lines from its left vertices meeting outside it. Redrawn 2026-11-09 and overlaid 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 250 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session); each side was checked by sampling the ink across it. The upper left vertex was 5 units right of the corner and the lower left one 2 units low, so that the two strokes left their vertices off the ink: the figure is redrawn through the ink, the lower stroke with the turn and loop it has on the page and the tail at the foot of the right side added. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: à gauche, un petit croquis : quatre segments issus d'un point, dans un cercle, deux d'entre eux repassés à l'encre
drawings.kind: segments from a point inside a circle
drawings.notes: From the heavy central point five segments, all starting at that point: two inked heavily (up left, up right), three thin (down left, down, down right; the last leaves the lower left of the central blot and bends slightly). Around it the circle, drawn as he drew it, in straight pieces: the left side runs from the heavy left stroke down to the down-left segment and on to the bottom, the lower right piece ends on the down-right segment, the right side starts on the heavy right stroke, and a separate piece at the top; the gaps on either side of the downward segment are his, and the circle is a polygon of pieces, not a closed round curve. Five segments leave the central point where the mark says four: settled on the page 2026-11-12, and the transcription now says so in a note after the mark (#145). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 250 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session); each stroke was checked by sampling the ink across it. The centre moved 0.6 unit, the down-right segment (up to 1.7 units off) and the left and right pieces of the circle (about 1 unit off) redrawn through the ink; the other strokes lay on their ink. Matches the facsimile.
drawings.disagreement: Five segments leave the central point on the facsimile (two inked heavily, three thin), not four.

drawings.description: croquis en marge gauche ; au-dessus, un premier croquis du même losange, raturé
drawings.kind: diamond x, y', y, z (Hasse diagram), set as a tikz-cd diagram
drawings.notes: Set in tikz-cd at the editor's request (#148: « correct, but use LaTeX to represent this diagram »): x on the left, arrows to y' (upper) and y (lower), and from each an arrow to z on the right; all four labels read on the 400 dpi colour crop, the same diagram as the tikzcd the transcription sets just above the mark. The tikz-cd layout is canonical: it keeps the shape of the margin sketch, not its geometry, so it is not overlaid on the crop. Left out, following the convention for strike-outs: the first sketch above it, heavily struck with zigzag hatching, and the horizontal stroke just above the diamond (a heavy cross at its left end, two small arrowheads), part of the struck first attempt (confirmed by the editor, #148). Not compiled (no TeX in the session).

drawings.description: en marge gauche, deux croquis. En haut, un segment oblique épais portant trois points marqués, avec les lettres $x$ (près du premier) et $y$ (près du troisième). En bas, un triangle aplati : à gauche les points $x'$ et $x$, en haut $y''$, $y$ et $y'$, à droite $z$ et $z'$ ; des traits joignent $x$ à $y$ et à $z$, $y$ à $z$, $y'$ à $z'$, et un trait fin $x'$ à $y''$.
drawings.kind: segment with marked points; flattened triangle x, y, z with outer points (transitivity)
drawings.notes: Top: the heavy oblique segment, three marked points on it (computed on the segment), the letter x under the first and y under the third. Bottom: the points x', x (left), y'', y, y' (top), z, z' (right) with their letters, and the strokes x'-x (heavy), x-y continued to y', x-z, y-z, y'-z', the thin stroke x'-y'' and a short stroke from y'' towards y. Left out: a small sign beside z (a struck letter or a second z), a short stroke under y (the tail of its letter). Record checked against its .tex header after the rebuild of 7b758b8 (all fields agree). Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the lower figure lay 2.5 to 3.5 units too high at the left and right (x', x, z, z'); its seven points are moved onto the blots of the page and every stroke redrawn between them; on the page the upper stroke starts at x and the right-hand strokes end at z (from y) and z' (from y'), which settles the two readings left open before. The transcription gives this figure as a row of labelled points in a displayed formula and describes it in the note; the mark is added beside it. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à droite, deux polygones : un hexagone dont le sommet supérieur gauche est marqué d'un gros point, et un second polygone plus petit, à cinq ou six côtés.
drawings.kind: two polygons, one with a marked vertex
drawings.notes: As on the page: a hexagon with a heavy point at its upper left vertex, and to its right a smaller polygon drawn with six corners (top, upper right, right, lower right, lower left, left), two of which (upper right and right) are blunt. Decided here: the second polygon is drawn with the six corners seen on the page; the note of the transcription calls it a pentagon, which it is if the blunt corner at the upper right is only a bend of the pen. Either way it is a polygon beside the hexagon, and the text (the list of faces in dimension 2) does not depend on the count. Record checked against its .tex header after the rebuild of 7b758b8 (all fields agree). Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop: both polygons fall on the page within a unit; unchanged. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: marge gauche, trois petits croquis l'un sous l'autre : en haut, un losange dont les sommets gauche et droit sont marqués ; au milieu, un faisceau de quatre flèches montantes, avec une tache et des points ; en bas, un éventail de cinq traits issus d'un sommet, terminés chacun par un point, dont le secteur de gauche est hachuré.
drawings.kind: three marginal sketches: a rhombus, a bundle of arrows, a hatched fan
drawings.notes: Top: a rhombus (top, left, bottom, right vertices), its left and right vertices heavy, and above it, from its top vertex, a quadrilateral of arrows: an arrow coming down to the top vertex from the upper right, a top side, an arrow down the right side, and an arrow back along the bottom to the top vertex. Middle: a blot with, below it, four arrows pointing upwards side by side (the last one oblique) and two dots, and above it three upward arrows (from the left of the blot, from the blot, and at the right) and a short oblique arrow; above them two arrows pointing left. Bottom: five strokes from one lower vertex, each ending in a point, drawn from the one vertex; the sector at the left is closed by a stroke from the first point down to a lower left corner and a stroke from that corner up to the second point, and cross-hatched (drawn as four strokes); a wavy stroke runs along the right-hand strokes. Record checked against its .tex header after the rebuild of 7b758b8 (it agreed). Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and corrected: the quadrilateral of arrows above the rhombus (part of the same sketch: it starts at the rhombus's top vertex) was missing, and lies above the old bbox (bbox extended up to 0.148, every coordinate moved 10 units down accordingly); in the middle figure the three upward arrows above the blot and the two leftward arrows were missing; at the bottom the closing strokes of the hatched sector were missing. Left out: the words of the text that run into the margin; small letters and digits beside the middle figure (a ringed letter above it, '-a' at its left, small 3s beside two arrow tips; not read); a long stroke rising at the right of the middle figure towards the word « connexité » (perhaps part of the word). Still differs: the hatching of the fan is free; the directions of the arrowheads of the quadrilateral are a reading of heavy short strokes. Not marked and not part of this drawing: a hatched fan of two crossing lines after « S A F » at the top of the page (x 0.37 to 0.45, y 0.2 to 0.27), and a short vertical bar with heavy ends in the left margin at « 2 sommets »: see the report. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 250 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the three sketches stand at their places, their strokes within about 1 to 2 units of the ink; nothing moved. Still differs, besides what is listed above: in the middle figure the arrows are drawn as straight single strokes, several of them 1 to 2 units off their ink and some of the page's arrows doubled; the hatching of the fan is free (four strokes for about six on the page).

drawings.description: marge droite, deux petits croquis : en haut, un éventail de quatre traits issus d'un sommet inférieur ; en bas, un polygone hachuré posé sur un sommet d'où partent aussi trois traits épais vers la gauche.
drawings.kind: two marginal sketches: a fan of four strokes; a hatched polygon on a vertex
drawings.notes: Top: four strokes rising from one lower vertex, drawn from that vertex. Bottom: from a vertex two triangles rise side by side, each with its apex at the top: the left one (vertex, a left corner, the left apex), the right one (vertex, the right apex, a right corner, and a straight side back to the vertex); a long stroke from the right apex down to the left runs across the left triangle; free hatching strokes in both (drawn as six strokes), a small dot under the right apex; and three heavy strokes from the vertex to the left, the lowest a short separate one. Record checked against its .tex header after the rebuild of 7b758b8 (it agreed). Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on the 400 dpi colour crop and redrawn: the earlier lower figure (one pentagon with three hatching strokes parallel to its left side, the heavy strokes fanning down to -91) did not match: the outline is two triangles from the vertex, the heavy strokes run to -78, -86 and -87. The tops of the upper fan moved 2 to 3 units up onto the page. Left out: the words of the text and the long oblique line of the crossing-out which pass through the crop. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128). Overlay check 2026-11-14 (claude-opus-5-5, issue 147): the 400 dpi colour rendering of the 250 ppi scan laid under the redraw, rasterised from its TikZ (not compiled: no TeX in the session); each stroke was checked by sampling the ink across it. The right side of the right triangle runs straight from the right corner to the vertex on the page (the earlier redraw had a corner 2 units outside the ink), and the side from the right apex to the right corner lay 1.3 to 1.8 units off: both redrawn on the ink, with the bottom of the left triangle and the six hatching strokes moved by up to 1.7 units onto their ink; the upper fan and the three heavy strokes lie on their ink. Still differs: the hatching is free, and a few short hatching dashes (one at the left of the left triangle, two at the upper right of the right one) are not drawn.
